GOLF CROQUET · 3D CLUB EDITION
WELCOME TO THE CLUB

Aim. Swing. Outplay.

  1. Aim: tap or click the lawn. The dotted line shows your chosen direction, with yard marks along the lawn. Each shot starts aimed toward your next wicket (or stake); click to change direction and fine-tune it yourself. In Shot view, the camera stays fixed while you aim; tap Shot view again to recenter. Fine-tune with the slider or ← → keys.
  2. Swing: on desktop, drag left across the long mallet pad and release. Hold Shift while dragging for five-times finer adjustment. On touchscreens, pull down and release. A longer pull means more power; yard marks are a ruler, not a recommended shot. Natural lawn grain and strike variation affect both sides. Short strokes are precise; powerful, long-range shots have more direction and distance uncertainty. The roll distance is an estimate. Keep the pull straight along its axis: sideways drift anywhere in the swing pushes the shot off line. Watch the swing marker and feedback. On desktop, hold and release Space for keyboard power control. Select Roll shot to switch to Jump shot: the ball launches at a fixed loft; power controls height and carry. It can clear another ball, clip a wicket, bounce, and roll after landing. A ball flying above the hoop does not score.
  3. Score: send the whole ball through its highlighted hoop in the arrow direction, or hit the highlighted stake when it is next in your sequence.
  4. Keep your bearings: the clock-tower pavilion always marks the north end of the lawn.
  5. Play tactically: knock opponents away, block a hoop, or set up your second ball. A knocked-through ball scores for its owner.

Game rules

Association and Backyard support 2, 3, or 4 players with one human. Two players use the usual two-ball sides. With 3 or 4 players, this app uses a club free-for-all: one ball each, Blue (you), then Red, Black, and Yellow (computers). First player to finish their ball’s course wins; bonus-shot rules still apply. This is a custom multiplayer format.
